topics.topic: AuditEntry identity and store-history namespace across restored histories
questions: Is an AuditEntry identified only by its sequence number within the currently restored store history, or must the model also identify the store history so entries with the same sequence number in different pre-loss and post-restore histories are distinguishable?

When a restored history later reuses sequence numbers that the lost history had written after the backup, is an AuditEntry identified only by its sequence number within the current store history, or must a store-history identity also distinguish entries across histories?

When a restored history reuses numbers that existed only in the lost post-backup branch, is an AuditEntry identified only within its store history, and if so what identifies or supplies that history namespace?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1 about AuditEntry identity across restored store histories.

precedent.topic: AuditEntry identity and continuity across restored store histories
precedent.why: Registry exposes only the current store history; lost-history entries cannot be read or acted on, and immutable backup entries have identical observable facts whether treated as the same entities or restored copies.

topics.topic: MigrationClosure identity and cardinality scope across restores
questions: Is the one-closure and one-successful-import limit per Registry instance across all restores, or per store history, allowing the same instance to acquire another MigrationClosure after restoration to a pre-import backup?

Is MigrationClosure cardinality at most one per store history, allowing the same production instance to acquire a new closure after restore and re-import, or at most one across the entire lifetime of the instance?

Is MigrationClosure scoped to the production instance or to one store history, and after a pre-import backup is restored and the import succeeds again, is the new closure the same logical value or a distinct history-scoped closure?

quotes:
Substitution: there is at most one, and two records of "the migration
succeeded at instant T" would mean the same thing.

Continuity: it is written
once and never changes; it is a fact about the instance, not a thing with a
life.
Durable, at most one per instance.

A store
restored after a loss from a backup made before the import begins a history
without it (R0-89).

A store lost before a checked backup holds the import
loses the import with it, and the import may then be made again: the owner
keeps the export file and the picks, names and aliases given in the import
until a checked backup holds the import, and retires the VPS instance only
then (R0-79).
judgement.why: M10 scopes its single immutable closure to the Registry instance, while R0-89 permits that same instance to lose the closure and create one again after restoring an earlier store history.

topics.topic: AuditEntry sequence high-water mark and first number after restore
questions: Does “the backup's last number” mean the persisted high-water mark of every sequence number ever written as of that backup, or the greatest audit entry still present in the backup after older entries have been erased?

What sequence number does the first new audit entry after restoration receive, and does “backup's last number” mean the highest number ever minted before that backup even when its entry had already been erased, or only the highest entry retained in the backup?

quotes:
Sequence numbers are never reused within a store's history (M09): changes
   that write an entry are applied one at a time, and each entry takes the
   number after the last that history ever wrote, kept in the store apart
   from the entries, so an erasure does not lower it. A store restored after a
   loss begins its own history from the backup's last number (R0-89).
judgement.why: State 2 specifies a separately stored high-water mark, so erasing entries does not lower it and the first new entry takes the following number.
